curriculum.lesson_evidence: Significant events have causes and effects that change people’s lives. Effects can be short or long term and can differ for different groups, including First Nations Peoples.
curriculum.scope_limit: Proposed Stage 2 NESA HSIE alignment using catalogue outcome codes (HS2-*); content-point mapping and local First Nations protocols remain pending human review.

lesson.child_mission: Significant events have causes and effects that change people’s lives. Effects can be short or long term and can differ for different groups, including First Nations Peoples.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same HSIE idea to a new place or source, then compare two pieces of evidence for strength.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
For a published event in your pack, name one cause and two effects for different groups if shown.

FEEDBACK
Answers depend on the event pack — must be evidence-based.

WATCH FOR
Assuming everyone experienced an event the same way hides unequal effects.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Complete three event effect webs from published sources. Explicitly note First Nations effects when sources provide them; otherwise mark “not in these sources”.

Write a short reflection naming one source or idea you corrected and why.
lesson.learning_intention: Significant events have causes and effects that change people’s lives. Effects can be short or long term and can differ for different groups, including First Nations Peoples.
materials: Optional: local map, photo or interview notes
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.
lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Complete three event effect webs from published sources. Explicitly note First Nations effects when sources provide them; otherwise mark “not in these sources”. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Sample: original example using event on new material; names a specific word, source or choice and explains its effect.

Parent: Written model 2: Sample error: Assuming everyone experienced an event the same way hides unequal effects.. Correction: Answers depend on the event pack — must be evidence-based.. Why it helps the audience is stated.

Parent: Likely misconception: Assuming everyone experienced an event the same way hides unequal effects. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating event on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with event, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

Parent: Marking notes: Accept original work about event with a specific supporting detail. Reject copied model wording with no new material. / Accept a misconception, a correction, and a purpose-linked reason for event. Reject corrections that do not change the inaccurate idea..

teach_steps.explain:
Significant events have causes and effects that change people’s lives. Effects can be short or long term and can differ for different groups, including First Nations Peoples.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner base claims on sources, places and respectful community knowledge, rather than guessing from a single picture. Keep every claim linked to evidence.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the sources, map features or community examples that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your record with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your evidence? If a detail is uncertain, identify what source you would need next. One deliberate, evidence-based revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
